subject: Biotechnology
title: Variants of Uncertain Significance
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Variants of Uncertain Significance.

hook.text: Your genome has 4 to 5 million variants — most are harmless, some cause disease, and many are just unknown.

buildup.text: ClinVar classifies variants from pathogenic to benign — but a huge fraction sits in the middle as VUS.

discovery.text: A VUS in BRCA2 might mean cancer risk or might mean nothing — the patient is stuck in diagnostic limbo.

twist.text: Population databases like gnomAD help — if a variant is common in healthy people, it is probably benign.

climax.text: Multiplexed assays of variant effect test thousands of mutations at once — resolving VUS at industrial scale.

punchline.text: Not pathogenic, not benign — VUS is genomics' biggest gray area.

quiz.question: How do population databases help reclassify variants of uncertain significance?
options: They sequence the variants more accurately than clinical labs
Variants found commonly in healthy populations are likely benign, helping reclassification
They provide treatment options for patients with unknown variants
